claim_tested: AlgJ is catalytically active as an SGNH enzyme
key_finding: AlgJ has a conserved D190-H192-S288 triad and shows acetylesterase activity in vitro
context: Purified AlgJ periplasmic domain; structure solved to 1.83 A (PDB 4O8V, which is the P. putida protein Q88ND3)
confidence_and_limitations: High for catalytic competence. Acetylesterase activity on a surrogate substrate does not identify the physiological acetyl donor or acceptor.

stance: refutes direct polymer acetylation by AlgJ
key_finding: AlgJ shows weak or no detectable polymannuronic acid binding; AlgX binds polymannuronate specifically and in a length-dependent manner
context: Defined-length polymannuronic acid, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
confidence_and_limitations: High. Measures binding of the unacetylated polymer by the isolated protein, so it cannot exclude polymer engagement within the assembled AlgJFXK complex.

claim_tested: AlgJ and AlgX differ in surface electrostatics
key_finding: AlgJ is structurally similar to the AlgX N-terminal domain but has a distinctly different electrostatic surface potential
context: Crystal structures of AlgJ and AlgX
confidence_and_limitations: High, reported qualitatively in the source paper and quantified independently here (C2).

claim_tested: AlgJ is a membrane-anchored periplasmic protein required for alginate acetylation
key_finding: AlgJ is required for O-acetylation in vivo; its N-terminal sequence is an uncleaved type II signal anchor rather than a cleaved signal peptide
confidence_and_limitations: High for the in vivo requirement and the anchor. Conflicts with the UniProt Signal 1-21 feature on Q88ND3.

claim_tested: algJ is required for alginate production and acetylation
key_finding: Basis of the IDA annotations GO:0051979 and GO:0042121 on P. aeruginosa AlgJ (Q51393)
confidence_and_limitations: High for the pathway requirement. A loss-of-function phenotype does not assign a molecular function to the protein.

claim_tested: Alginate modification and export proteins form a complex
key_finding: Crystal structure of the AlgK-AlgX complex; AlgKX binds alginate oligosaccharides directly and complex formation is required for polymer production and biofilm attachment
context: Paper framed on P. aeruginosa; deposited entry 7ULA is built from P. putida KT2440 AlgK (Q88NC7) and AlgX (Q88ND0)
confidence_and_limitations: High for AlgX-AlgK. AlgJ is absent from the structure, so the AlgJ-to-AlgX hand-off is not observed.

claim_tested: The AlgJ catalytic triad and oxyanion hole are complete and geometrically competent
key_finding: Ser288 OG to His192 NE2 = 2.56 A; His192 ND1 to Asp190 OD1 = 2.74 A; oxyanion donors Tyr289 N (2.59 A), Thr287 OG1 (2.66 A), Thr287 N (3.35 A) to a modelled oxyanion position
context: Experimental 1.815 A structure of the target protein
confidence_and_limitations: High. Geometry is from the apo enzyme; no acyl-enzyme or substrate complex exists.

claim_tested: AlgJ differs from SGNH enzymes with known polymer acceptors in active-site charge
key_finding: Net formal charge within 12 A of the catalytic Ser OG: AlgJ -7, versus -1 to +1 for all five enzymes with a demonstrated polyanionic polymer acceptor (AlgX x2, PatB x2, OatA-C) and 0 and -3 for two hydrolases whose acceptor is water
context: Deposited coordinates; residue counts within 12 A are 44-58 across the panel
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Formal charge ignores pKa, ions and solvent screening; n = 8 means AlgJ ranking first carries p = 0.125 under label exchangeability, so this is a described outlier, not a significance test.

claim_tested: The triad, oxyanion hole and acidic patch are conserved across alginate producers
key_finding: D190, H192, T287, S288, Y289, D235, E343, E94 and R347 are identical in 20 of 20 sequences including Azotobacter vinelandii O52197; E314 and D315 vary (K314/E315 in P. aeruginosa)
context: UniProt AlgJ orthologs, 35.0 to 93.2 percent identity to Q88ND3
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. Pairwise Needleman-Wunsch rather than a curated multiple alignment; one 35 percent entry may be a fragment.

citation: This work, Q88ND3 sequence and AF-Q88ND3-F1-v6
claim_tested: AlgJ has a single N-terminal membrane anchor and a periplasmic catalytic domain
key_finding: One Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy maximum (GRAVY 1.27) centred at residue 13, span about 4-22; residues 1-6 MTRTLR give 2 basic and 0 acidic, fitting the positive-inside rule for Nin-Cout; the crystallised domain is 75-370
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. AlphaFold pLDDT is 95.7 and 96.4 for the two catalytic lobes but 68.9, 67.6 and 52.1 for residues 28-60, 61-78 and 266-278, so the model does not place the active site relative to the membrane.

claim_tested: The two chains in 4O8V form a biological dimer
key_finding: The A-B contact buries 16 residues per side across 91 heavy-atom contacts below 4.0 A and the two catalytic serines are 20.5 A apart
context: Crystal form of the AlgJ periplasmic domain
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Interface size fits crystal packing; no solution oligomeric-state measurement was available to this analysis.

claim_tested: Existing GO annotation captures AlgJ function
key_finding: Q88ND3 has three IEA annotations (GO:0042121, GO:0005886, GO:0042597) and no MF term; GO has no alginate O-acetyltransferase activity MF term, only the BP GO:0051979
context: EBI QuickGO annotation and ontology APIs
confidence_and_limitations: High as a database state readout, retrieved 2026-11.
